title: T-53 evidence, two players merged: the member has the HOST's logistics plan copy open on the game's own plan pane with the warehouse dropdown open; a fresh bundle of the host's plans arrives (the old copy is replaced); the member then picks ITS OWN warehouse through the dropdown's own option select. Decides whether the pick is refused because the pane still holds the replaced object (no longer a known display copy -> own-plan test -> planSet elsewhere -> refused at the MPPatches 'logistics plan warehouse' line). Control: the same pick with no bundle in between must be accepted. Ends dissolved, NO save
preconditions: Fixture save1 (host melaus, client Client1). Dev build with DevT53.cs (`logpane` lever) deployed on the CLIENT. FIXTURE: the host's headquarters holds at least one logistics plan (not a factory plan) - its first row in `plans <host> rows logistics` is the one used; the client truly owns at least one warehouse that no other plan already targets (asserted: `warehouses` own=[...] and the pane's dropdown offers it). The screen is the game's own: `logpane open` runs BizMan.Open(<plan HQ>, LogisticsManagers) and the pane's own LoadPlan with the display copy; `logpane dropdown` is the dropdown's own middle-box click; `logpane pick` is the dropdown's own SelectOption, whose listener is the pane's OnChangedWarehouse (the gated method). The fresh copy is forced by `paperwork push` on the host (one publish, no plan edit). Leg B runs BEFORE the control leg A, because an accepted pick routes a warehouse change that would make the same option already-selected on a later leg. NOTHING is saved.

steps.note: both worlds settled (host's own line, client's snapshot apply) before the merge
the client settled before the merge (step 5); step 13 re-checks it is still settled after the merge
